collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager's new rain channel sends the water into a neighbor's hut: ask an elder to look, or talk it over.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) dug a little channel to carry the rain away from (subject.his/her) hut. It works perfectly. The water now runs straight downhill into (friend)'s hut instead. After last night's rain, (friend) woke up with a puddle under (friend.his/her) sleeping mat.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) climbs the hill with (friend.his/her) wet mat over (friend.his/her) shoulder. (subject) looks at the mat, then at the channel, and says, "Oh no." (subject.He/she) fills in the bottom of the channel that same morning and spends the afternoon helping (friend) dry everything in the sun. The next time it rains, both huts get a little wet. That, they agree, is fair.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (elder), an elder, walks up and down the slope, following the channel, and suggests turning it at the bottom so the water runs into the gardens instead. (subject) and (friend) dig the new bend together. The water goes to the beans. The beans are delighted. Nobody is wet.
